nodes.title: The title bar
nodes.detail: The operating system's frame is switched off and replaced by a 32px bar: a drag region with a label, and minimise, maximise and close buttons wired straight to the Tauri window.

anatomy.why: The label is a placeholder. The product name, snecko, is set in tauri.conf.json but never reaches the window, so every user sees the word 'app'.

nodes.title: The sidebar
nodes.sub: Resizable · holds the vaults and the tree
nodes.detail: A column down the left that holds the vault switcher and the file tree. Its right edge is a 4px handle you can drag, and right-clicking its empty space opens the New Note / New Folder menu.

nodes.title: Dragging its edge
nodes.detail: The width has a minimum and no maximum: the sidebar can be dragged across the whole window, over the editor.

rows.title: Press on the handle
rows.detail: A 4px strip on the right edge sets a resizing flag. Nothing moves yet.

rows.title: Width follows the pointer
rows.detail: Every mousemove on the window sets the width to the pointer's x, but never below 200px.

rows.title: No upper bound
rows.detail: The clamp is Math.min with a single argument, which returns that argument — so there is no maximum.

rows.title: Release anywhere
rows.detail: mouseup on the window clears the flag.

code.detail: `Math.min(Math.max(e.clientX, minWidth))` — the outer Math.min was meant to take a maximum as its second argument, and has none.

nodes.title: The vault switcher
nodes.sub: Pick, add or remove a vault
nodes.detail: A vault is just a folder. The switcher lists the ones you've added, opens one on click, adds one through a folder picker, and shows a remove button on every vault except the open one.

nodes.title: Adding a vault
nodes.detail: The new vault is opened straight away, but it is never remembered as the last vault: restart the app and the previous one opens instead.

rows.title: A folder picker opens
rows.detail: pickDir asks Tauri for one directory. Cancelling returns nothing and nothing happens.

rows.title: Added to vaults.json
rows.detail: addVault skips a folder that is already listed, and names the vault after the folder's last path segment.

rows.title: Opened straight away
rows.detail: openVault reads the folder's whole tree and shows it.

rows.title: Not remembered as the last vault
rows.detail: openVault looks the path up in `vaults` — the React state from before this add, which does not contain it yet — so setLastVault is skipped.

nodes.title: Opening a vault
nodes.sub: The whole folder tree, read up front
nodes.detail: Opening a vault reads every folder and note in it before anything is shown, however deep the tree goes.

rows.title: Every folder is read
rows.detail: readDir walks the tree recursively, one directory listing per folder, skipping any name that starts with a dot.

rows.title: The tree is replaced
rows.detail: The result replaces the file tree in one go; folders start collapsed even though their contents are already loaded.

rows.title: Remembered as the last vault
rows.detail: Only if the path is found in the vault list held in React state at that moment.

code.detail: `vaults` here is the state captured when this function was created. Called right after setVaults — on add, and at startup — it still sees the old list.

nodes.title: Removing a vault
nodes.detail: Removing a vault is meant to forget it if it was the last one opened. It never does: the check compares an object with a string.

rows.title: Only for vaults that aren't open
rows.detail: The switcher shows a check mark, not a remove button, on the open vault — so App's branch for removing the open vault can't be reached from the UI.

rows.title: Dropped from vaults.json
rows.detail: removeVault filters it out of the list.

rows.title: Meant to forget it as the last vault
rows.detail: It reads lastVault as a string and compares it with the path, but setLastVault stores a {path, name} object. The comparison is never true, so lastVault is never cleared and a new one is never chosen.

rows.title: Next launch opens nothing
rows.detail: If the removed vault was the remembered one, startup finds it missing from the list and opens no vault at all.

code.sub: Compares an object with a string
code.detail: `store.get<string>("lastVault")` — but lastVault is written by setLastVault as a Vault object. The type argument is a cast, not a check, so `lastVault === path` is always false.

code.sub: Unreachable branch for the open vault

nodes.title: Coming back where you left off
nodes.detail: On launch the app reopens the last vault, then the last note — but only if the note's path is inside that vault.

rows.title: Vaults and the last vault are read
rows.detail: Both come from vaults.json.

rows.title: The last vault reopens
rows.detail: Only if it is still in the vault list.

rows.title: The last note reopens
rows.detail: Only if its path starts with the vault's path; otherwise the editor stays empty.

nodes.title: The file tree
nodes.detail: Every folder and note in the vault except dot-names, folders first and then alphabetical, shown without file extensions. Folders expand on click — but their contents were already read when the vault opened.

nodes.title: Ordering and naming
nodes.detail: Each level is sorted on every render: folders before notes, then by name. Names are shown without their extension.

rows.label: Sorting
rows.value: in place on the array it was given, then copied

code.detail: `entries.sort(...)` reorders the array App holds in state before the copy is made. Harmless today, because nothing else reads that order — but it mutates React state outside setState.

nodes.title: Opening a note
nodes.detail: Clicking a note first writes any save still waiting for the note you're leaving, then loads the new one.

rows.title: A pending save is flushed
rows.detail: If a save timer is still running, it is cancelled and the current note is written immediately.

rows.title: The note is read
rows.detail: The whole file is read as text.

rows.title: It replaces the editor's text
rows.detail: The editor swaps its entire document for the new text.

rows.title: Remembered as the last note
rows.detail: setLastFile writes {name, path} to vaults.json.

nodes.title: The right-click menu
nodes.sub: On a note, or on the sidebar
nodes.detail: The browser's own menu is switched off for the whole window, and this one replaces it. Right-click a note for Open in new tab, Rename and Delete; right-click empty sidebar for New Note and New Folder.

anatomy.why: Global and unconditional: no right-click anywhere in the window — the editor included — shows the browser menu, so copy and paste are keyboard-only.

nodes.title: On a note
nodes.sub: Two of three items do nothing
nodes.detail: Open in new tab and Rename are in the menu with empty handlers. Only Delete does anything.

rows.to: nothing — onClick is empty, and App passes onRename: () => {}
asks to confirm, then removes it from disk

nodes.title: Deleting
nodes.detail: A native confirm, then the file — or the folder and everything in it — is removed from disk. If the open note was inside, the editor is cleared.

rows.title: Confirm
rows.detail: A blocking browser confirm: 'This cannot be undone.'

rows.title: Removed from disk
rows.detail: Recursively for a folder. There is no trash or undo.

rows.title: The editor is cleared
rows.detail: If the open note was the one deleted, or lived inside the deleted folder.

rows.title: The whole vault is re-read
rows.detail: The tree is rebuilt from disk.

nodes.title: On the sidebar
nodes.sub: New Note · New Folder, at the vault root
nodes.detail: Both create at the top of the vault, never inside a folder: the sidebar menu always passes the vault's own path, and the note menu has no 'new here'.

rows.to: Untitled.md, or Untitled N.md — then opens it

nodes.title: The note editor
nodes.detail: A CodeMirror editor that hides markdown's marks except on the line you're typing on, saves as you type, and shows the note's name as a button you click to rename it.

nodes.title: Typing and saving
nodes.detail: Every change is written back to disk 10 milliseconds after the last keystroke — in practice, at almost every pause — as a full overwrite of the file.

rows.title: CodeMirror reports a change
rows.detail: Its update listener passes the whole document text up on every edit.

rows.title: App takes the text
rows.detail: It becomes `content` in App's state.

rows.title: A 10ms timer restarts
rows.detail: Each keystroke cancels the previous timer, so a write happens 10ms after you stop.

rows.title: The whole file is overwritten
rows.detail: writeTextFile replaces the note on disk with the full text.

anatomy.why: The other direction: when App's `content` changes — opening another note — the editor's whole document is replaced. Typing doesn't trigger it, because the text already matches.

nodes.title: Live preview
nodes.sub: Marks hidden off the cursor's line
nodes.detail: Headings, bold, italic and inline code are styled where they stand; their #, * and ` marks are hidden on every line except the one the cursor is on.

rows.title: Rebuilt on change
rows.detail: On every edit, scroll or cursor move.

rows.title: Only what's on screen
rows.detail: The markdown syntax tree is walked within the visible ranges only.

rows.title: Styled in place
rows.detail: Headings 1–6, bold, italic and inline code get a class each.

rows.title: Marks hidden
rows.detail: #, *, _ and ` are replaced with nothing — unless the cursor is on that line.

code.detail: An anonymous class handed to ViewPlugin.fromClass. It holds the current decorations and rebuilds them when the document, viewport or selection changes.

nodes.title: Markdown styling
nodes.sub: Configurable in code, not in the app
nodes.detail: Heading sizes, weights and code styling come from one config object turned into a CodeMirror theme. The editor can swap it live, but nothing in the app ever changes it.

nodes.title: Renaming a note
nodes.detail: The note's name above the editor is a button. Click it, type, and press Enter or click away; the extension is kept and the file is renamed on disk.

rows.title: Click the name
rows.detail: It turns into a text field with the name, minus its extension.

rows.title: Enter or click away
rows.detail: Either submits; Escape cancels.

rows.title: Extension put back
rows.detail: An unchanged or empty name does nothing.

rows.title: Renamed on disk
rows.detail: Then the whole vault is re-read and lastFile is updated to the new path.

nodes.title: vaults.json
nodes.detail: Tauri's store plugin, loaded once and shared. The file sits next to the app's executable, which is found by a one-line Rust command because the JavaScript path API didn't work (the comment in lib.rs says so).

rows.label: lastVault
rows.value: Vault — written as an object, read once as a string

rows.label: Writable once installed?
rows.value: not guaranteed — install folders are often read-only

code.detail: A #[tauri::command] — the only Rust code the app adds. The comment above it: 'executableDir doesnt work so this is a workaround'.

nodes.title: Your notes on disk
nodes.sub: Plain files, read and written in place
nodes.detail: Notes are ordinary .md files in the vault folder, read and written whole. The app's file permissions allow reading, writing, renaming, creating and deleting anywhere on disk.

anatomy.why: Every file permission is scoped to `**`, not to the vaults you've added. The webview can touch any file the user can.
